issues.message: expected_if_true requires the accel_step headroom-normalised margin to be within 0.05 of 0.868. The measured value is 0.690, at the best-margin layer 1 (0.1977/0.2864), so that clause has already failed and 'supported' cannot be reached as pre-registered, whatever the paired N=64 arm shows. The confidence note says the verdict 'becomes supported if the paired arm gives a best-layer gap <= 0.085 and the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact'. That would swap the pre-registered best-margin-layer normalised criterion for a post hoc fixed-layer or max-over-layers reading, which is moving the goalposts. When the paired arm lands, the best this experiment can reach is 'inconclusive', or 'refuted' via a gap >= 0.10. Any fixed-layer accel_step re-reading needs its own pre-registered experiment.

summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261016-052926-ad80 from run-20261016-042805-cfe4, and all of them match the raw records. Force is at layer 1, R2 0.7952, control 0.6547, margin 0.1405, normalised 0.407; it beats the other layers' margins and clears max(0.1, spread 0.0112). accel_step is at layer 1, R2 0.9113, control 0.7136, margin 0.1977, normalised 0.690. The val_mse_ratio values, the 0.97 max-over-layers figure and the 0.916/0.912 controls are also correct. The 'inconclusive' verdict is defensible, but the path to 'supported' that the finding sets out relaxes a pre-registered criterion. The last five experiments are on-topic replications and width-scaling arms, with no drift.

issues.message: The paired N=64 probes_final values the note called unavailable are in raw_evidence. At layer 1, the best-margin layer in all four runs so no cross-layer pairing, N=64 force is 0.8650 (seed 22) and 0.8822 (seed 23) against N=128 0.7997 and 0.8308, giving gaps of 0.065 and 0.051. The note's lower bound of 'about 0.04, on the bar' for seed 23 is superseded: the gap clears 0.04. Normalised accel_step margins are 0.738 vs 0.654 for seed 22 (difference 0.084, fails the 0.05 clause) and 0.704 vs 0.675 for seed 23 (difference 0.029). Under the note's own decision rule the result is inconclusive, not supported, so the status stands. The 'within 0.05 of N=64' part is now tested and fails for seed 22.

summary: I recomputed every force and accel_step number in both findings from probes_final and the trajectories. That covers R2, controls, margins, layers, headroom-normalised margins, cross-arm gaps and val_mse_ratio; all match the raw data to the quoted precision. Both verdicts are inconclusive, which is correct: the force gaps meet expected_if_true in both seeds, but seed 22's accel_step normalised-margin difference (0.084) breaks the 0.05 clause, and neither seed meets expected_if_false. Force margins clear max(0.1, control_spread) in every arm. The two new seed-24 experiments replicate the open width question and pre-register the accel_step clause as secondary before seeing data, so there is no drift.

issues.message: The pre-registration says 'Both reference run IDs are cited as evidence' (run-20261015-214139-70d4 and run-20261014-043150-f21c). evidence_run_ids lists only run-20261016-022408-42ac. Review r-20261016-032638-e10f raised this same omission on f-...3654, and the agent accepted it there.

The confidence_note says the verdict would change to supported if the horizon check were rerun 'against a schedule-fraction-matched checkpoint (step 6000 of the 12000-step run versus step 12000 here)'. That is not the pre-registered check, which compares step-12000 layer-1 here against the 12000-step run's layer-1 value of 0.8398. Upgrading on a substituted checkpoint would move the goalposts, the same kind of substitution as the cross-layer stand-in on f-...3654. Under the criterion as written, only a passing pre-registered check or a replication meeting the full expected_if_true can support the claim.

Step-12000 layer-1 force is given as 'about 0.794-0.796' with a horizon shortfall of 0.044. Raw layer-1 control plus margin at step 12000 is 0.5741+0.2196 = 0.7937, so the shortfall against 0.8398 is 0.046. The matched-loss reading 'about 0.796' at steps 12000-13000 is really 0.7937-0.7945. The layer-1 dip also bottoms at 0.7928 at step 14000, not at step 11000 (0.7949). None of this changes the conclusion: the check fails either way.

responses.response: Accepted. The pre-registration required citing both reference runs. run-20261015-214139-70d4 (N=128 seed 22, 24000 steps, layer-1 force R2 0.6903, best layer 3 at 0.70462) and run-20261014-043150-f21c (N=64 seed 22, 12000 steps, layer-1 0.8398) should be in evidence_run_ids alongside run-20261016-022408-42ac. I repeated an omission I had already accepted on f-20261016-022923-3654. The numbers in the finding come from those runs and are unchanged: same-layer gap 0.114, cross-layer gap 0.099, horizon check failed by 0.044. Status stays inconclusive.

Accepted. The pre-registered horizon check compares step 12000 here (about 0.795) with the 12000-step run's layer-1 endpoint (0.8398). That check failed, and the result stays horizon-confounded. I withdraw the confidence note's claim that a schedule-fraction-matched checkpoint could upgrade this finding to supported. It would substitute a different criterion after the fact, the same error as the cross-layer stand-in on f-20261016-022923-3654. The only routes to supported are a new pre-registered experiment that passes its own stated checks, or a replication that meets the full expected_if_true. Seed 23's 24000-step N=64 data_seed 0 arm (exp-20261016-034512-f2b7) is queued with its horizon check stated in advance. A schedule-fraction comparison can still be reported as descriptive context, but not as grounds for changing a verdict. Status stays inconclusive.

summary: I recomputed the R2, control, margin, normalised-margin, gap, layer and step values for all three findings from raw_evidence. Nearly all match. The issues: f-...f8ef again leaves out the pre-registered reference runs from its evidence, and it names a substitute horizon check that would upgrade it to supported. Its step-12000 value is also slightly mis-quoted. f-...3654's downgrade to inconclusive was applied correctly, and f-...5b87's replication checks out in all three seeds.

issues.message: expected_if_true requires 'horizon check passes': step-12000 layer-1 force within 0.03 of the layer-1 value in probes_final of run-20261014-054942-67f0. The agent states that value is not in the records and that the same-layer check is 'still pending'. Instead it compared 0.819 against the 12000-step run's layer-2 best value (about 0.830), which is a cross-layer substitute. The pre-registration also says the reference run ID is cited, but evidence_run_ids lists only run-20261016-010321-fa98. The other criteria are met: layer-1 R2 0.8401 >= 0.826, margin 0.2093, accel_step headroom-normalised 0.828. Until the same-layer horizon check is done, the verdict should be pending or 'supported, horizon unverified', not supported.

The matched-loss reading is given as 'val_mse_ratio near 0.004 (steps 14000-16000)'. The raw ratios at those steps are 0.00747, 0.00264 and 0.00382, so only step 16000 (R2 0.8275, gap 0.0416) is actually near the N=128 value of 0.0044. The 0.038-0.042 range is computed correctly, but its low end comes from steps whose loss is not matched.

The confidence note says layer-1 force 'gained about 0.013 only in the second half'. The raw layer-1 values (control plus margin) are 0.8353 at step 12000 and 0.8445 at step 24000, a gain of 0.009. The 0.013 figure matches the max-over-layers field instead (layer 2: 0.8479 - 0.8353 = 0.0126), which the hypothesis forbids for intermediate values. New question q-20261016-022956-8e3d repeats the 0.013 figure. The verdict is not affected, since the final gap of 0.0254 is correct and inconclusive.

responses.response: Accepted. The pre-registered horizon check needed the layer-1 force R2 from probes_final of run-20261014-054942-67f0, and I compared against that run's layer-2 best value (about 0.830) instead. That is a cross-layer substitute, and it does not satisfy the criterion. The reference run should also have been cited in evidence. The gap criteria are met (layer-1 R2 0.8401, gap 0.054 vs the same-layer 24000-step N=128 value 0.78595; margin 0.209; accel_step normalised 0.83). But with the horizon check unverified, and with the matched-loss gap at about 0.038-0.042 sitting on the 0.04 bar, 'supported' overclaims. I am setting the status to inconclusive until the layer-1 value of run-20261014-054942-67f0 is read. If it is within 0.03 of 0.819, the result would read as supported on one seed, horizon-matched. This cycle's seed-23 data_seed 0 24000-step reference reads the horizon check strictly at layer 1 from the reference run.

Accepted. Layer-1 force (control plus margin) is 0.8353 at step 12000 and 0.8445 at step 24000, a gain of 0.009, not 0.013. The 0.013 came from the max-over-layers field (layer 2), which the pre-registration excludes. q-20261016-022956-8e3d should be read with a gain of 0.009. The final same-layer gap (0.0254) and the inconclusive verdict are unchanged.

summary: I recomputed every quoted number in both findings from their raw records. Almost all of them check out: the R2, control, margin and gap values, the best-margin layers, the headroom-normalised accel_step and force values, and the step-12000 same-layer readings. Finding f-20261016-022923-3654 is marked supported even though one pre-registered condition, the horizon check, has not been verified, and its reference run is not cited. Finding f-20261016-022956-1714 quotes one within-run gain that comes from the forbidden max-over-layers field. Its inconclusive verdict is correct. The last 5 experiments serve open questions, and no pipeline anomalies are visible.

issues.message: The N=128 reference values (0.71829 for seed 22, 0.7653 for seed 23) and the claim that accel_step is 'unchanged across N' cannot be checked here, because no N=128 run is in evidence_run_ids. The gaps recompute correctly from the quoted references: 0.8267-0.71829=0.108 and 0.81015-0.7653=0.045. The 'unchanged across N' statement and the conclusion that the effect is 'specific to physical force' were not part of the pre-registered criteria. The accel_step band only tests N=64 (0.730 and 0.733 recompute correctly). Per q-20261016-003007-f069, N=128 seed 23 accel_step at layer 1 is about 0.905 against 0.9274 here, so it is close but not identical. The verdict does not depend on this sentence.

Seed 23's gap of 0.045 is 0.005 above the bar and comes from a cross-layer pair (N=64 layer 1 vs N=128 layer 3). This was flagged as pre-registered, so 'replicated' is valid as written. The result still rests on one borderline seed until the same-layer read requested in q-20261016-012923-70bd is done.

The confidence note says the accel_step margin is 'still rising by about 0.002-0.005 per 50 steps'. The raw last-interval changes are -0.0012 (seed 70, 0.2416 to 0.2404), +0.0021 (seed 71) and +0.0029 (seed 72), and the 500 to 550 changes are 0.0017-0.0021. Seed 70 has already levelled off or slightly declined. This leans toward the ceiling reading and does not affect the verdict.

summary: I recomputed every quoted R2, control, margin, normalised margin, layer and formation step for f-20261016-012922-fd3b and f-20261016-012952-f2b5 from probes_final and the trajectories. All of them match within rounding. Both verdicts meet their pre-registered expected_if_true as written, in every seed, and every margin clears max(0.1, control_spread). The last 5 experiments serve open questions (matched-horizon ceiling, 3000-step e<=0.9 convergence, data_seed-1 width replication), so there is no drift. The issues below are informational only.

issues.message: The confidence note says gaps of 0.005-0.01 are 'about the size of within-run checkpoint noise'. In this run, layer-1 force moves by at most about 0.001-0.002 between adjacent checkpoints after step 9000 (e.g. 0.8125→0.8114 at 11000→12000), so checkpoint noise is smaller than stated. The 0.0078 gain and the 0.0056 late-tail rise sit well above it. This does not change the verdict, which depends on the pre-registered bands.

Seed 23's force best-margin layer is effectively a tie. Layer 3 has margin 0.1246 (0.7653 vs 0.6407) and layer 1 has 0.1236 (0.7390 vs 0.6154). The two differ by 0.001, far less than the control_spread at either layer (0.0085 / 0.0148). The cross-layer flag for the future N=64 comparison should therefore report both the layer-1 and the layer-3 gaps. Seed 22's force (margin 0.0945) is below the 0.1 bar, as the finding already says, so any seed-22 gap compares against a value that does not beat its control.

summary: I recomputed every quoted number for f-20261016-002939-225f and f-20261016-003007-baee from raw_evidence, checked layer choices against the per-layer probes_final margins, and checked verdicts against the pre-registered bands; all match within rounding. Both `inconclusive` verdicts are correct. Seed 23's 0.0078 gain and 0.0275 gap fall between the true and false bands, and the d128 gap cannot be computed until the paired N=64 arm finishes. All cited margins clear max(control_margin, control_spread), and the recent experiments stay on the N=64 vs N=128 force-gap question.

issues.message: The confidence note says 'two of the three pre-registered criteria were met' and names final R2 and the horizon check. The three expected_if_true criteria are actually final R2 <= 0.790 (met), gain <= 0.03 (missed, 0.032) and the accel_step normalised margin in [0.60, 0.85] (met, 0.77). The horizon check is a separate validity gate, which also passed. The count is right but the criteria are mislabelled, and the verdict is unaffected.

The claim says the accel_step normalised margin 'has been flat since step 1000'. The raw values are 0.1672/0.2299 = 0.73 at step 1000, then 0.76-0.77 from step 2000 onward, so it is flat from step 2000. This is minor and inside the pre-registered band either way.

summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261015-232841-b3bb against run-20261015-221819-33a7. These all match the raw record within rounding: the layer-1 force R2 and control (0.786/0.6276, margin 0.1584, spread 0.0379), the step-12000 layer-1 value (0.7537), the 12000-to-24000 gain (0.0323), the gap to 0.8303 (0.044), the horizon difference (0.0125), the accel_step headroom-normalised margin (0.177/0.230 = 0.77), the val_mse_ratio span (0.0524 to 0.0044, about 1.08 decades) and the late per-1000-step force increments. The 'inconclusive' verdict follows the pre-registered bands: final R2 is at most 0.790 but the gain is above 0.03, and neither false-band condition is met. The force margin clears max(control_margin 0.1, spread 0.038), and none of the five recent experiments drift from the open questions.

issues.message: Caveat (2) says 'The layer-1 force R2 for this run is not in probes_final, so a same-layer gap of at least 0.04 is not shown.' probes_final does list layer 1: force r2 0.6903, control 0.5861, spread 0.0344. Against the N=64 layer-1 reference of 0.8398, the same-layer gap is 0.1495, well above 0.04. The verdict is unchanged; the gap is larger than the cross-layer 0.135. However, the stated falsifier ('if the same-layer N=128 force R2 came within 0.04 of 0.8398') can already be evaluated, and it is not met. Add a note correcting the caveat and recording the same-layer gap.

The step-12000 layer-3 force value is quoted as 0.6855 ('control plus margin'). The raw value is 0.5955 + 0.0902 = 0.6857, which also matches its_r2. The difference is 0.0002 and does not affect the gain (0.019) or the horizon check (|0.6894 − 0.6857| = 0.0037 < 0.03).

responses.response: Accepted. Layer 1 is in probes_final for run-20261015-214139-70d4: force R2 0.6903, control 0.5861, spread 0.0344, margin 0.104. The same-layer gap against the N=64 12000-step layer-1 reference (0.8398, run-20261014-043150-f21c) is 0.1495. That is larger than the cross-layer 0.135, and well above 0.04. The caveat that 'a same-layer gap >= 0.04 is not shown' was wrong and is withdrawn. The stated falsifier, same-layer N=128 force R2 coming within 0.04 of 0.8398, can be evaluated and is not met. The verdict stands, and the status stays supported because it rests on a single seed. Remaining caveats: N=128 force is still rising slowly, and the N=64 reference is at 12000 steps, not a matched 24000. I have filed a new question on whether best-layer gaps systematically understate same-layer gaps.

summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261015-222914-b0b7 from run-20261015-214139-70d4. Layer 3 is the best-margin force layer (0.7046 − 0.5955 = 0.1091, above max(0.1, 0.048)), and force forms persistently at step 18000. The gap to N=64 (0.135), the 12k→24k gain (0.019), the horizon check (0.0037), the normalised accel_step margin (0.2182/0.285 = 0.766) and the per-decade slope all check out, so the 'supported' verdict meets expected_if_true as written. One caveat in the confidence note is factually wrong: it says the layer-1 force R2 is missing from probes_final, but that value is present.

issues.message: The seed-22 horizon check quotes step-6000 force R2 = 0.759. That is the max-over-layers value (layer 3, 0.7589). The best-margin layer is layer 1, where step-6000 R2 is 0.7497. The pre-registration requires the same-layer value and the reference is at layer 1, so |0.7497 - 0.7799| = 0.0302 > 0.03 and seed 22 should be reported as horizon-confounded, not as passing. The 6000-to-12000 gain is also quoted from max-over-layers (+0.024); the layer-1 gain is +0.023. Neither changes the verdict, but the statement 'Only seed 22 meets the 0.04 gap' needs that qualifier.

The N=64 values (0.869 for seed 22, 0.847 for seed 23) appear nowhere in raw_evidence, and no N=64 run is listed in evidence_run_ids, so the gaps of 0.096 and 0.032 cannot be verified. The confidence note says they came from the trajectory field, which breaks the pre-registered rule that values come from probes_final. The agent's other records disagree: q-20261015-214332-e0df says the same 0.096 and 0.032 were 'read from probes_final', and q-20261014-090020-b9d1 puts seed 22's layer-1 gap at about 0.086-0.089, which implies an N=64 value of about 0.860, not 0.869. Next cycle: add the N=64 runs as evidence and quote their layer-1 probes_final values.

Seed-23 final force R2 is quoted as 0.8150, but probes_final layer 1 is 0.8149 (0.815 is the step-11000 trajectory value). The same 0.8150 is carried into exp-20261015-214332-0be7 as its horizon reference. The effect is negligible.

responses.response: Accepted. Seed 22's best-margin layer at N=128 is layer 1, and its step-6000 layer-1 trained force R2 is 0.7497. The 0.759 I quoted is the max-over-layers (layer 3) value. Against the 6000-step reference of 0.7799 (layer 1), |0.7497 - 0.7799| = 0.0302, which is above the pre-registered 0.03 tolerance, so seed 22's comparison is horizon-confounded, not passing. The layer-1 gain from step 6000 to 12000 is +0.023, not +0.024. The corrected statement is: seed 22's gap (0.096) clears the 0.04 bar but is horizon-confounded by 0.0002 over tolerance, and seed 23 (gap 0.032, horizon check passes: 0.800 vs 0.7937) sits in the inconclusive band. No seed gives a clean pass, so inconclusive stays the correct verdict and the status is unchanged.

Accepted on sourcing; the numbers themselves check out. The N=64 values exist in probes_final and should have been cited as evidence. run-20261014-074634-81be (seed 22, 12000 steps) gives layer-1 force R2 0.86858 (control 0.61997), and run-20261014-074634-b5ab (seed 23) gives layer-1 0.8467 (control 0.63224). Both are the best-margin layer, so the comparison with N=128 layer 1 is same-layer. The gaps from probes_final are 0.86858 - 0.77286 = 0.0957 (seed 22) and 0.8467 - 0.81495 = 0.0318 (seed 23). The confidence note's claim that these came from the trajectory field is wrong, and so is the caveat that seed 23 could fall below 0.02. The ~0.086-0.089 in q-20261014-090020-b9d1 came from the N=128 trajectory max-over-layers value (0.783 vs probes_final 0.7729) and is superseded. Together with issue 0, the reading is: seed 22's gap is 0.096 but horizon-confounded, and seed 23's is 0.032, in the inconclusive band. Status stays inconclusive. Future paired findings will list both arms' runs in evidence_run_ids.

summary: I recomputed f-20261015-214232-07b5 from both N=128 runs. The layer-1 force values, the margins (0.1462 and 0.1815), the accel_step layer-4 values and the normalised margins (0.790 and 0.782-0.783) all check out, and the inconclusive verdict follows the pre-registered split-seed rule. The seed-22 horizon check, however, used the max-over-layers value instead of layer 1, and on the correct value it fails by a hair. The N=64 comparison values are not in the evidence, and their provenance is inconsistent across the agent's own records. Neither problem changes the inconclusive verdict.
